owner: Next independent QA/load wave; root coordinates source/runtime review
question: Identify actual owner/lifecycle of checked-out sole connection while /api/auth/me or token identity waits. Existing stack identifies waiters only.
isolation: New owned receipt-backed UUID on existing private PG55483, restricted nonowner/NOSUPER/NOBYPASS role, real migrated current schema. No shared roles/HBA changes and no inference-based cleanup.
source: Exact accepted source to be chosen at start; preserve hash map, Python/package/config fingerprints before/after. No accidental schema31 relabel.
instrumentation: Use a separate harness; do not change production sources before reproduction.
Record SQLAlchemy pool checkout/checkin plus request/task/thread correlation and bounded own-module caller frames; no SQL parameters, tokens, identity, payload, raw request URL or health data.
Record _do_get timing and a snapshot of current holders when an acquisition starts/fails. Timing and waiter stack alone never attribute a holder.
Preserve private raw output with public projection and hashes; a bounded pool timeout makes a failed replay finite. Mark instrumentation overhead and timeout delta.

Exercise actual supported factories and natural /api/auth/me + stats or equivalent R12 browser overlap. Explicit artificial delays must be identified separately and cannot establish causality for the historical run.
bounds: Short controlled single-/two-request or existing browser replay; no CPU/PDF/load campaign while another Chrome/VM/load runs. Coordinate root first.
acceptance: First preserve natural failure or honest inability to reproduce; identify holder with direct ownership receipts. If product fix is warranted, make smallest causal change, show same failing criteria pass, preserve tenant reset/auth revocation/restricted-role and one-connection behavior, then independent review. Never claim pool20/10 resolves deadlock.
SLO: Business arrival-rate, deployment hardware/workers/DB connection budget and p95 objectives remain to agree; no universal capacity or production extrapolation from local reads.
